title: Campaign
description: content/campaigns/*.json. Mirrors packages/shared/src/types/chapter.ts Campaign; where the two disagree the TypeScript type wins. A campaign is a story arc of 4-8 chapters and the unit of the carryover commitment rule (spec §6, §8.2). A campaign with `graph` is a graph campaign (#192, docs/campaigns/graph-campaigns.md): its next chapter is chosen by the graph's edges rather than by chapter index. Without `graph` it is an ordered campaign, read exactly as before.

_note.description: Author-facing note that survives into the shipped JSON. Ignored by the loader.

chapters.description: Every chapter file in the campaign, including every member of a routed beat. Each must exist under content/chapters/. For an ordered campaign the set of distinct `index` values must run 1..n with no gaps, and a routed index must cover its route set exactly — checked by tools/content/validate.mjs. For a graph campaign every listed chapter must be played by some node and no chapter may declare a `route`; `index` is not read.

routeSets.description: Named sets of story flags a routed beat chooses from, e.g. the three roads north, or the three pursuits. Declared here rather than inferred from the files that exist, because the failure worth catching is a *missing* member: only a declared set can notice an absence.

setbackLimit.description: Setbacks before the campaign fails — spec §8.3's 'fails at three setbacks, tunable per campaign'. Absent means 3.

purseBackfill.description: Campaign.purseBackfill: the purse for an attempt saved before the party purse existed. `coins` is the base; `byFlag` adds an amount per carried route flag the attempt holds.

requires.description: Campaign.requires (#221): campaign ids the household must have finished before this one can be started. Met by a `complete` attempt at each (any ending, a loss ending included); a failed or abandoned attempt does not count. Absent means no prerequisite. Each id must name a campaign that exists, and prerequisites must not form a cycle - content:validate and the loader check both, since only the whole set can say.

graphId.description: A node or edge id. Stable: saved attempts name it, so renaming one is a content migration.

graph.description: CampaignGraph (packages/shared/src/types/campaign-graph.ts). Optional and versioned: absent means an ordered campaign. Every name in it must resolve (parseCampaignGraph), checked by tools/content/validate.mjs and at server startup.

version.description: The declaration version. This build reads 1 and refuses any other.

entry.description: The node a fresh attempt starts at.

nodes.description: The places, keyed by stable node id, in authored order.

edges.description: The ways between places, keyed by stable edge id. A node's exits are offered in this order.

flags.description: Journey flags beyond routeSets members: seeded into every chapter run of the attempt and read back when its chapter completes.

facts.description: World facts (#198): typed, bounded, attempt-scoped values the journey carries beside its flags — a place displaced or restored, a threat sleeping or cleared, favours owed, a road open. Written by edge effects and node onComplete rules, read by guards and variants. Keyed by stable fact id, in authored order.

buffs.description: Temporary buffs (#200): guard, damage, movement or roll bonuses (or burdens) rift energy can grant for a few turns or fights. Granted by the grantBuff effect, stored on the attempt's journey, applied only inside fights. Keyed by stable buff id.

graphBuff.description: BuffDef (packages/shared/src/types/buffs.ts). Bounded on purpose: amount within the kind's limit (guard 3, damage 2, move 2, roll 3; parseCampaignGraph checks the per-kind bound), at most 5 turns, fights or uses. A roll buff may opt in to story checks instead of attacks (appliesTo: check, #222); parseCampaignGraph checks that such a buff lasts a number of uses, targets the party and that spend appears only with it.

label.description: What the screens call it, for an 8-year-old.

amount.description: Per stack. Negative is a burden: the cost side of a tradeoff.

target.description: party (default): every hero. one: the hero holding the story turn when the fight begins.

oneOf.description: A story-check buff's clock (#222): the next count checks it is spent on. Only with appliesTo: check.

cap.description: The most this buff can add (or take away), however it stacks.

expiresOn.description: chapter (#222): the next chapter played ends, however it ends.

appliesTo.description: Roll buffs only (#222): attack (default) - attack rolls in fights, as before; check - one story check (d20 + stat vs TN) instead, never an attack, held by the party and spent by whoever rolls.

spend.description: With appliesTo: check only (#222): auto (default) - spent on the party's next check; choose - the roller's phone offers it first, to spend now or save.

chapter.description: The chapter played here; a member of the campaign's chapters.

revisit.description: Entering after this node completed: replay (default) plays it again, pass walks through to the exit choice, closed forbids it.

variants.description: A different chapter for this place when its condition holds. First match wins, on every entry that plays the node.

revisit.description: Re-entering the (completed) node while this variant is the place: replay or pass, overriding the node's revisit (#198).

onComplete.description: Completion rules (#198): when the node's chapter completes, every rule whose `when` holds (read after the outcome is recorded and the journey flags read back) applies its effects, in order.

ending.description: Makes this node an ending: completing its chapter completes the attempt. An ending has no exits.

kind.description: forward: onward. sideways: a neighboring place at the same point in the story. return: back to somewhere the story has been, which is what makes a cycle intentional.

locked.description: Unavailable until an unlock effect opens it.

once.description: May be taken once per attempt.

irreversible.description: The author's claim that there is no way back to `from` after taking it. Checked by tooling, shown as a warning; not enforced.

blocked.description: How the exit is drawn while unavailable. hidden (default) or shown.

rift.description: Makes this edge a rift (#196): a stateful link with a lifecycle (dormant, open, closed, consumed, expired, collapsed). Absent means an ordinary edge. See docs/campaigns/graph-campaigns.md, Rifts.

fallback.description: The long way round (#197): offered only while no other exit from `from` is available. Keeps a party a used-up, collapsed or shut rift strands moving.

graphRift.description: GraphRift: composable rift properties, every one optional. {} is a rift open from the start, forever.

oneWay.description: The promise that no rift leads straight back. Checked by tooling, shown by the screens.

uses.description: Crossings before it is consumed. 1 is single-use. One crossing is one party-wide move.

lasts.description: Timed: expires once count ticks of unit have passed since it opened. visits = places entered; chapters = chapters completed (the session clock). Turn timing is #201's.

opensWhen.description: Triggered: dormant until this holds. Unless persistent, crossable only while it holds.

unstable.description: Deterministic instability: a flicker rhythm on visits to `from`, and/or collapse after a number of crossings.

flicker.description: Open on `open` visits to `from`, then gone for `shut`, repeating.

persistent.description: Once open, open for good. Cannot also be uses, lasts or unstable.

linkedTo.description: The partner rift: two mouths, one shared state. Must link back and declare the same lifecycle.

reveal.description: When the destination is shown. always (default), when-open, when-crossed.

redirects.description: Where else the rift can be turned to lead (#197): a redirectRift effect or a party's redirect action names one of these (or `to`). Not on a linked rift.

actions.description: What the party may do to this rift while choosing at its `from` (#197). Each kind present is offered while its rule's `when` holds and the action would change something. A kind may be one rule, or a list of ways to take it (#199), each with its own `id`, `when`, `requires` and effects.

riftActionRules.description: One rule, or a list of ways to take the same rift action (#199): every way in a list needs an `id`, distinct within it (RIFT_ACTION.way names it) - checked by parseCampaignGraph.

riftActionRule.description: RiftActionRule (#197): when the party may take one rift action, what its button says, and what else it does. `when` reads the journey (the lint walks it); `requires` (#199) reads the seated party and is checked by the server, never by a guard.

id.description: Which way this is, when the kind lists several (#199). Stable: a stored lastAction names it.

hint.description: What a party that cannot take this way is shown (#199). Absent: the way is not drawn for them. Must not name a hidden destination; needs `requires`.

partyRequirement.description: PartyRequirement (#199): who in the seated party can take a rift action. Every field present must hold; within a list, any one will do. Checked by the server against the seated party, never by a guard; the lint proves the campaign stays winnable without it (CLASS_GATED_ONLY_PATH).

anyClass.description: Someone seated is one of these classes.

anyItem.description: Someone seated carries one of these items (content/items.json ids; inventory or quest items).

graphCondition.description: GraphCondition: every field present must hold. Reads the journey only, never the party.

outcome.description: How the subject node's most recent completion ended: the edge's `from`, or a variant's own node.

visit.description: The subject node's visit ordinal is within these bounds (inclusive): on an edge, the visit to `from` being finished; on a variant, the visit being begun; in onComplete, the visit completing.

facts.description: World facts, each tested: a bare value (equals), or { in, not, min, max } — every key present must hold. A fact never written reads as its initial.

oneOf.description: Sets a world fact (#198) to a value in its domain.
Moves a counter world fact (#198) by a non-zero integer, clamped to its bounds.
Acts on a rift (#197): discover (drawn while blocked, destination revealed), open (latched), close, stabilize (no flicker, collapse or expiry). A final rift is left as it is.
Turns a rift (#197) toward its own `to` or one of its declared `redirects`.

Grants a declared temporary buff (#200), or refreshes, stacks or ignores one already held as its stack says. firstCrossing (#222, an edge's own effects only; parseCampaignGraph checks where): grants only on the edge's first crossing this attempt (a rift's first, by either mouth of a linked pair).

worldFact.description: WorldFact (packages/shared/src/types/campaign-graph.ts). An enum (one of 2-12 states), a counter (integers min..max, span at most 20) or a flag. `domain` groups it for the tools and screens; `visible` shows it to the players.

factValue.description: A world fact's value: an enum state, a counter's integer, a flag's boolean.
